newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, ignore Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, ignore Dow rebound.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Monday, ignoring a rebound in New York as investors grabbed profits in Canada's largest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 43.17 points, or 0.7 percent, to close at 6154.54. Trading was heavy with 89.2 million shares changing hands worth C$1.46 billion ($1.06 billion).
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average shrugged off early losses to finish the day with a 20-point gain.
"The overall tone of the (TSE) is weak and sloppy at the moment. We're seeing some profit taking here," said Joe Ismail, a technical analyst at Maison Placements Canada.
While the Dow appeared to shake off fears of a hike in U.S. interest rates, Canadian financial markets remained nervous on Monday.
The Bank of Canada intervened to support a weak Canadian dollar which was hit by concerns about how the central bank will react to a possible U.S. rate move.
Banks and other interest-rate sensitive stocks are expected to be volatile this week, Ismail said.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-groups, 12 ended weaker led by a 139-point loss in precious metals. The TSE's strength was in consumer products and base metals.
Declining stocks outpaced advances 661 to 346 with 266 issues unchanged.
* Among the banks, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce fell 0.25 to 67, while Bank of Montreal dropped 0.55 to 52.25.
* Western Star Trucks Holdings Ltd. sank 1.70 to 37.50 after the company forecast lower earnings due to problems at its Orion Bus unit.
* Petro-Canada was the most-active stock, slipping 0.10 to 19.90 on 6.3 million shares.
* Corby Distilleries Ltd. was the top gainer, up 1.20 to 44.20 in light trading.
